pos.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger's Arsenal wanted the ball and dominated through quick passing possession, though the 2003-04 side was also lethal on the break with Henry.

pro.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger's teams played out on the ground with fast one-touch passing and took risks to break lines, while still hitting quick vertical balls for runners like Henry.

est.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger gave attackers freedom to move and combine (Henry drifting wide, Bergkamp dropping, Pires and Ljungberg coming inside) rather than drilling fixed zones.

lar.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger's Arsenal attacked through intricate central combinations with wide players tucking inside, rarely relying on wingers crossing.

blo.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger's teams defended in a compact mid-block 4-4-2 with a fairly high line rather than an aggressive high press or a deep low block.

mar.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger's sides defended zonally, including his often-discussed zonal marking at set pieces, and he did not assign man-markers to stars.

pla.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger was famously committed to his own way of playing and reluctant to adapt to opponents, even in big games against stronger rivals.

res.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger saw football as an art meant to entertain and kept attacking rather than shutting games down.

sis.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger trusted the intelligence and talent of his players, giving stars like Henry and Bergkamp freedom over rigid tactical drilling.

jog.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger prized technique and creative playmakers (Bergkamp, Fabregas, Ozil, Cazorla) while also valuing athletic power and pace (Vieira, Henry).

bas.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger trusted and developed young players (Fabregas, Wilshere, Henry and Vieira as young signings), mostly bought young rather than built from the club's own academy.

lid.personaBrief: No verified evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Wenger led as a calm, trusting educator who protected his players and favoured a united group over iron-fist discipline, while keeping the final say.
